'''John Hyslop Steele''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FRSE|size=100%}} (15 November 1926 – 4 November 2013) was a British [[Oceanography|oceanographer]] who made major contributions to the study of [[Marine ecosystem|marine ecosystems]].<ref name="Telegraph">{{cite news | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/10599939/John-Steele-obituary.html | title=John Steele - obituary | work=The Telegraph | date=27 January 2014 | accessdate=13 February 2014}}</ref><ref name="Globe">{{cite news | url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/12/04/john-steele-falmouth-oceanographer-formerly-directed-woods-hole-oceanographic-institution/Wn4bY29ljscoU1n0StIV6M/story.html | title=John H. Steele, 86, of Falmouth; oceanographer formerly directed Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution | work=The Boston Globe | date=4 December 2013 | accessdate=13 February 2014 | author=Lawrence, J M}}</ref><ref name="RSE">{{cite web | title=Dr John Hyslop Steele FRS FRSE | website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh | date=28 October 2016 | url=https://www.rse.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/steele_jh.pdf | format=PDF | access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref>

==Work==
In 1951 Steele began work at the Marine Laboratory in [[Aberdeen]], Scotland.
He was appointed director of the [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]] in 1977.<ref name=Telegraph /><ref name="RSE"/>
After his retirement from Woods Hole in 1989, Steele continued his interests of research and served on the boards of the [[Bermuda Institute of Ocean Sciences]], the [[Exxon]] Corporation, and the [[Robert Wood Johnson Foundation]].<ref name=Telegraph />

==Awards==
* 1963: Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref name=Telegraph /><ref name="RSE"/>
* 1973: [[Alexander Agassiz Medal]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=Telegraph /><ref name="RSE"/>
* 1978: Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref name=Telegraph /><ref name="RSE"/>
* 1978: Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=Telegraph />

==Life==
Steele was born 15 November 1926, in [[Edinburgh]].<ref name=Telegraph /> He was educated at [[George Watson's College]], and graduated from [[University College London]] in 1946.<ref name="RSE"/> In 1956 he married Evelyn and they had one son.<ref name=Telegraph />

Steele died 4 November 2013, at his home in [[Falmouth, Massachusetts|Falmouth]], Massachusetts.<ref name="RSE"/>
